annotations.text: CALM — the state the product is in almost all the time. If this looks alarming, parents stop trusting it.
RED — has to be readable from the doorway, in the dark, out of the corner of your eye.
REVIEW — one item at a time, in arrival order. The queue is strictly first-in-first-out: only the front item can be acted on, so no direction offers a pick-any list.

CHOSEN 2026-08-30: direction B, Console. Shaked's reason - the built app needed to read as real desktop software, and B is the direction that does. A and C stay here on purpose: nothing is locked, and Yahli has not reacted yet.

Read DOWN a column to judge one direction. Read ACROSS a row to compare the same moment three ways.

No 'Got him' / 'Mute' button, deliberately. Nothing in the backend can acknowledge or silence an alert that is happening now - confirm/dismiss/skip are about what an OBJECT is, not about an alert in progress. Rather than draw a button that does nothing, the alert stays informational and clears itself when he moves away. Making acknowledgement real means adding it to the backend first.
